::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 16th [1898]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Devon Record Office, Exeter 53/10/9/1
:::

My dear [Edmund](people/person_42.qmd)
Thank you for the result of your audacious bit of sacrilege, and also Mr Hardy.   Mr Bowland’s epitaph, I am glad he was a keeper of the parks and not of the swine!  [Duthy](other_books/otherbook_737.qmd) read the name Bockland and [Marsh](other_books/otherbook_734.qmd) Bowland[^1]  He must have been a man in good odour with employers and tenants  I wonder whether his eulogy is the work of a Bishop’s Chaplain or a college fellow  I should think it unusual to give his name in plain English, and the age and date were elaborated pieces of work

So many curious things have turned up since I began about the history of Hursley and Otterbourne that I think it will be very entertaining

Thanking you much
your affectionate cousin
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The research was  connected with her book *John Keble’s Parishes*, in which she quotes, 19-20, the Latin epitaph of John Bowland (d.1474). Morshead, who taught classics at Winchester College, may have provided the translation.
